## Hive 0.3.0 — the open pull requests of your project, next to the terminal
The right panel now has a PRs tab that lists the open pull requests of the repository of the project you are looking at.
### New
- **PRs tab** (⌥⌘P): next to "Pedidos", it lists the open pull requests of the project's GitHub repository, grouped by what needs your attention: review requested from you or one of your teams, your own PRs with something pending, the rest, and drafts (collapsed). Each one shows its stage (conflict, CI failed, changes requested, CI running, approved, waiting for review), the checks, how long ago it was updated, and a link that opens it on GitHub. - It uses the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`) that you already have signed in. For each organization, Hive uses the `GH_CONFIG_DIR` of its profile; an organization without one uses your machine's default `gh` account, and the tab says so, with a shortcut to set up an account for that organization. - The panel is 320 pt wide and is available even when agent delegation is off. In that case the Pedidos tab explains it and takes you to the organization profile. - The tab you picked is remembered. When the panel opens with a request waiting for you, it opens on Pedidos.
### Improved
- The window widens to fit the panel when it is too narrow, and gives the width back when you close it.
### Security
- Hive only reads from GitHub: it never creates, comments, approves or merges anything. - It asks GitHub only while the PRs tab is on screen, Hive is the active app and its window is visible (about every 60 seconds, every 20 seconds while a check is running). It does not ask with the panel closed, on the Pedidos tab, in the background or with the window minimized. - Only the `GH_CONFIG_DIR` of the organization profile reaches `gh`. A `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN` in the environment where Hive was opened, and the variables and secrets of the profile, are not passed on. Hive stores no token and keeps the pull request data in memory only. - This is the first network traffic Hive starts besides the update check.
### Known limits
- It needs `gh` installed and signed in, and only repositories on github.com are listed. - To tell which review requests are for your teams, `gh` needs the `read:org` permission. Without it, requests to teams are shown in their own group, with the command to grant it. - If you add an `origin` to a project while Hive is open, the tab notices it after you switch to another project and back. - Not yet verified: using the list with VoiceOver and with the keyboard only (Return and Space on a row), two different GitHub accounts side by side, and a missing `gh`. The 50 most recent pull requests are shown.
---
*Hive is made by Zeep Labs.*

## Hive 0.2.0 — agents that can hand work to each other (BETA)
Claude Code agents opened by Hive can now ask another agent in the same organization to do a task, and nothing is sent until you approve it.
### New
- **Agent delegation (BETA, off by default)**: turn on the agent delegation switch in an organization's profile. Claude Code sessions of that organization that you open from Hive afterwards can list the other Claude Code sessions of the same organization, ask one of them to do a task, send an informational mention, and check the result. - **You approve every request**: each task or mention waits until you approve it, edit it and approve, or reject it. Only then does Hive type it into the other agent's terminal, and only when that agent is idle and has no unsent text in its prompt. - **Board dos Agentes** (⌥⌘B): a board with the requests by state (waiting for approval, queued, in progress, done, ended). **Requests panel** (⌥⌘P): a side panel that shows what is waiting and lets you send simple requests without leaving the terminal. The sidebar shows which agents have a request waiting.
### Fixed
- The orange "waiting for input" dot no longer appears after an agent has been idle for about a minute. Claude Code sends a reminder notification at that point, and Hive used to read it as the agent needing you.
### Security
- Delegation never crosses organizations, and an organization with the switch off gets no Hive tools in its sessions. - Each session gets its own private local channel that only exists while the session is open. Hive does not change your Claude Code settings or the organization's Claude config folder; the Hive tools are added to your own MCP servers, not in place of them. - That channel only accepts connections from processes that belong to the session itself, and refuses a second connection, so another agent running on your Mac cannot speak for a session that is not its own. - The status signals that Claude Code sends to Hive (working, waiting, finished) are accepted only from the session they name, so another agent on your Mac cannot fake them to push a request into an agent that is not ready. - Task text and results are kept in memory by Hive only and are discarded when Hive closes. The database keeps only who asked whom, the state and the dates. Claude Code itself still saves what it receives and what it is asked in its own conversation history on your disk, as it does for anything else you type to it.
### Known limits
- Only Claude Code takes part. Codex and opencode do not. Agents opened outside Hive are not seen. - Changing the switch affects only sessions opened afterwards; sessions already open keep working as before. - A request can wait in the queue if the other agent is working, has text typed but not sent, or its status is not known yet. Pending requests and their text are lost when Hive closes. - Hive knows about unsent text only from what you type, paste or drop into its terminal, and stops counting it after 10 minutes without activity. Text that ends up in the prompt another way, or sat there longer, can be sent together with a request. - The limit of 3 chained requests is a guard against runaway loops, not a security barrier: your approval of each request is. Turning the switch off does not end delegation in sessions that are already open. - The reply to a rejected request only says it was rejected by you; the reason you type is not sent to the agent. - Delegation is a beta. Not yet validated: the warning shown when the switch changes, the light system theme, narrow windows, VoiceOver, a very long request in a small window, and a quick double click on Send or Reject. - The interface is in Portuguese.
---
*Hive is made by Zeep Labs.*

## Hive 0.1.2 — restore a session, back to the same conversation
When an agent ends, you can now go back to the exact conversation it had, not just start a new one.
### New
- **Restore session**: when a Claude Code, Codex or opencode panel ends, or after you quit and reopen Hive, the panel offers a restore button (labelled in Portuguese) next to Reopen. Restore opens the same agent in the same conversation; Reopen still starts a new one. Hive saves only the conversation id the agent uses, never its content. - If a conversation can't be restored (for example it was deleted), the panel says so and Reopen becomes the main action.
### Fixed
- Agents installed in common folders such as Homebrew or `~/.local/bin` are found even when the shell started by Hive doesn't have those folders in its PATH.
### Known limits
- Codex only gets a restorable conversation after you send its first prompt. Two Codex panels in the same project, both without a saved conversation, may offer only Reopen until one of them ends. - A conversation started in a plain shell tab, or by another agent process in the same folder outside Hive, is not tracked. - Restore uses your current organization profile. If the conversation lives in another organization's settings, it fails and Reopen is offered. - "Reabrir todas" (reopen all) always starts new conversations. - The interface is in Portuguese.
---
*Hive is made by Zeep Labs.*
